note: NCB only: National Commercial Bank is Jamaica's largest bank and card issuer; Scotiabank Jamaica's and JMMB's card schedules weren't reached in this pass. NCB's card rates and charges (personal cards, effective 1 December 2025), read in full, with its fee guide effective 1 September 2026 for the two annual fees it changed: its five personal cards, the Visa Classic, Visa Platinum and Mastercard Platinum Travel in Jamaican dollars and the Mastercard and Mastercard Platinum Travel in US dollars, each with its joining and annual fee for the primary card (the Visa Classic's 4,800 and the Mastercard Platinum (JMD)'s 14,800 from the September 2026 guide, the others from the December 2025 schedule), its unsecured annual interest rate range, written at the top with the bottom as the lowest (the Mastercard's secured rate of 15% isn't written), a cash advance fee of 7.5% (plus GCT, at a rate not stated, so not added), a cross-border conversion fee of 1.25% to 3%, written at 3%, a monthly minimum payment of 4% of the statement balance, and its late payment, over-limit and returned cheque charges (which include GCT). No grace period is stated. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) added Scotiabank Jamaica, one of the country's two largest banks, whose rates and fees pages a plain request reached: its credit card interest rates page and its credit card fees page, read in full. Its personal cards in Jamaican dollars (Scotiabank Mastercard, Gold, MAGNA and AERO Platinum Mastercard; Visa Classic, AAdvantage and Gold Visa; The Platinum Card American Express, single currency) and the Platinum Mastercard in US dollars: each card's annual interest rate on purchases, a range set on approval, written at its top with its bottom as the range's lowest; its annual membership fee; the minimum payment (5% of the balance, at least J$300, or 3% on the AERO Platinum; 3%, at least US$75, on the Platinum Mastercard); an interest-free period of at least 21 days on purchases when the statement is paid in full, written as 21; and the rate after a missed minimum payment, up to 54.99% on Jamaican dollar cards and 24.99% on US dollar cards, written as the penalty rate. On the Visa and American Express cards the fees table also gives the late payment and over-limit charges, the ATM cash advance fee (7.30%, at least J$493.56; 9.87% in a branch, not written), the returned cheque charge and, on the Visa cards, a 2.50% cross-currency conversion fee; the Mastercard table gives none of these, so none is written for those cards. The Mastercard cards' US dollar side, the dual-currency Platinum Card (the same terms as the single), the business cards and the ScotiaLine (a line of credit) aren't written. Tried and not used: JN Bank's site refused the request (406), Sagicor Bank's sits behind Cloudflare, and JMMB's card pages weren't reached. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) also added CIBC Caribbean, one of the region's largest banks, whose Jamaica schedule of charges for cards (effective may, 2022, last updated july 2026) its site now serves (an earlier pass found it refused or not linked): read in full, its personal credit cards (14), each with its annual fee for the primary card (none where the schedule gives 0.00 or Free; waived for the first year where the schedule says so), its yearly purchase rate, its cash advance rate and fee, its late payment, over-limit and returned cheque fees, the minimum payment where the schedule gives one, and its late payment rate as the penalty rate, as the earlier CIBC files do. Its business, corporate, commercial and Bizline cards aren't written, nor the replacement, statement, rush card, emergency payment and auto-payment charges, which a holder meets only by asking or by an auto-payment; the UWI cards are for the University of the West Indies' students, faculty and alumni, a condition the game doesn't check. It states no grace period or foreign transaction fee. The Senior or Local Only Visa Classic is for seniors or for use in Jamaica only, conditions the game doesn't check.
